literal: Non-killing goodness-having-it is penance; others' evil not-speaking goodness-having-it is noble character.
translation: The virtue of penance consists in the goodness of not killing; the virtue of noble character consists in the goodness of not speaking of others' faults.
modern: பிற உயிர்களைக் கொல்லாத நற்பண்பே தவ வலிமையாகும்; பிறருடைய குற்றங்களைப் பேசாத நற்பண்பே சால்பு என்னும் சான்றாண்மையாகும்.
explanation: This couplet defines two high spiritual and moral ideals by comparing their core qualities. The strength of penance or self-discipline (நோன்மை) lies in the supreme goodness of non-killing (கொல்லா நலத்தது), which means refraining from causing harm to any living being. In a parallel way, the perfection of noble character (சால்பு) lies in the goodness of not speaking about the faults or evils of others (பிறர் தீமை சொல்லா நலத்தது). Just as an ascetic guards against physical violence, a noble person guards their speech against verbal violence and gossip.
